correctness.rationale: For every real \(C^2\) curvature-radius perturbation with zero mean and first harmonic, positivity and closure give exact perimeter \(2\pi\). The squared chord norm admits an integrably dominated second derivative, and rotational invariance diagonalizes the quadratic form. Explicit two-angle averaging yields elementary trigonometric integrals and a nonnegative squared-sine integral. An odd-harmonic-sum recurrence evaluates the latter exactly; positivity follows from an explicit rational bound with numerator \(16m^4-18m^3-33m^2+23>0\) for each integer \(m\ge2\). Odd harmonic sums grow logarithmically, giving the sharp \(2/m^2\) leading spectral weight. CHECK.py tests exact polynomial integrals for frequencies 2–15 and direct geometric central differences. These finite checks do not prove the unrestricted result.

value.rationale: For mean distance between independent arclength-uniform boundary points, the disk is the classical fixed-perimeter maximizer. Its full exact second-variation spectrum resolves sensitivity to every infinitesimal curvature harmonic, proves strict modewise local stability, and identifies the sharp inverse-square frequency law \(Q_m\sim2/m^2\). This structural all-frequency law explains why smooth convex-body stability can be weak against curvature oscillation; it is not an arbitrary finite calculation.
